objectives: “This course is addressed to teach student how to use Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to identify the phase composition, possible impurities, as well as crystallite sizes and crystal defects in their synthesized compounds. It is aimed to give a good understanding of the basics of diffraction on powder-like materials.“
content:
“1.) Brief history of X-ray invention and invention of X-ray diffraction (XRD)
2.) Instrumentation: X-ray sources: X-ray diffractometers for powder XRD (PXRD); X-ray detectors
3.) Basics of elastic scattering of X-rays on matter
4.) Fourier Transform as a covenient mathematical tool for understanding diffraction effects
5.) Bragg equation and indexing of X-ray powder patterns
6.) Structure factors: calculation of the Bragg peak intensities of simple cubic lattices (FCC, BCC); multiplicity factor of a powder diffraction
7.) Line profile analysis of PXRD: determination of crystallite size and crystal defects
8.) Concept of reciprocal lattice and the Ewald construction; Application to 2-dimensional lattices
9.) Determination of impurities and quantitative phase analysis in multi-component systems“
books:
“(Theory)
1.) A. Guinier ““X-Ray Diffraction““ (in Crystals, Imperfect Crystals, and Amorphous Bodies)  1963
2.) B.E. Warren ““X-Ray Diffraction““ 1990
3.) J. Als-Nielsen ＆ D. McMorrow ““ Elements of Modern X-Ray Physics““ 2001
(Practical Use)
1.) A. Taylor ““X-ray Metallography““  1961
2.) C. Suryanarayana, M. Grant Norton, “X-Ray Diffraction A Practical  Approach”, 1998.
3.) V.K. Pecharsky and P.Y. Zavalij, “Fundamentals of Powder  Diffraction and Structural Characterization of Materials”, 2005.
4.) B.D. Cullity ＆ S.R. Stock ““Elements of X-Ray Diffraction““, 2001“
